styles.description: Styles, periods, movements and cultures with a distinct visual character.

techniques.name: Processes and Techniques
techniques.description: Processes applied to a material or an object that set its look: charring, plastering, gilding, dyeing.

effects.name: Conditions and Effects
effects.description: Physical conditions of a surface, made on purpose or by time: charred, patina, weathered, crackle.

materials.name: Materials
materials.description: Substances and the species of natural materials: wood, sugi, lime plaster, bronze.

design_elements.name: Design Elements
design_elements.description: Motifs and ornament added to an object or a building: acanthus, putti, meander, rocaille.

objects.name: Objects

The effect is characteristic of the style.

architecture.description: Buildings, landscapes and urban spaces as built form: exteriors, massing, roofs and structure.

interior.name: Interior
interior.description: Interior spaces as composed wholes: layout, wall and floor finishes, furnishing and decoration.

furniture.name: Furniture
furniture.description: Movable furnishings for sitting, lying, storage and work, seen as individual designed objects.

lighting.name: Lighting
lighting.description: Light fixtures and the lighting of spaces, where light is the focal point.

decorative-arts.name: Decorative Arts
decorative-arts.description: Functional and ornamental objects of craft materials.

fashion.name: Fashion
fashion.description: Clothing and personal adornment as worn.

visual-design.name: Visual Design
visual-design.description: Visual communication in print and on screen.

film.name: Film
film.description: The cinematic image and the designed worlds of screen and stage.

styles.name: Classical
styles.description: Architecture of ancient Greece and Rome built on the classical orders (Doric, Ionic, Corinthian), with columns, pediments, entablatures, strict symmetry and proportional systems.

sources.title: Ancient Greek Dress: The Classic Look
Greek
sources.publisher: Fashion History Timeline (Fashion Institute of Technology)

architecture.markers: Temple fronts of fluted Doric, Ionic or Corinthian columns carrying entablature and triangular pediment, stepped stylobate, marble or stone, strict symmetry; Roman arches, vaults and domes.

sources.title: Classical (AAT 300020093)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

sources.title: Greek Architecture: Everything You Need to Know
Roman Architecture: Everything You Need to Know

furniture.markers: Klismos chairs with curved backs and saber legs, couches (kline) with turned legs, diphros and X-frame folding stools, tripod tables, bronze fittings, animal-leg supports.

sources.title: Is the klismos chair the most ancient piece of furniture still in rotation?

fashion.markers: Draped rectangles of wool or linen: chiton pinned at the shoulders, peplos with overfold, himation or white toga wrapped over a tunic; fibulae, girdles, sandals.

fine-art.markers: Marble and bronze nude or draped figures, contrapposto stance, idealized proportions, calm faces, clinging wet-look drapery, relief friezes; veristic Roman portrait busts.

variants.name: New Classical
variants.description: Contemporary practice (from the 1980s) of classical and traditional architecture, promoted by bodies such as ICAA and INTBAU, using the orders, symmetry and traditional materials in new buildings.
variants.markers: New buildings using correct classical orders, porticoes, pediments and symmetry, load-bearing stone or brick, traditional proportions, cornices and multi-pane sash windows.

styles.name: Byzantine
styles.description: Eastern Roman architecture (c. 330–1453): centralized plans, large domes on pendentives, round arches, and interiors sheathed in gold-ground mosaics, marble revetment and icons.

sources.title: Byzantine (culture and style) (AAT 300020669)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

sources.title: Heaven and Earth: Art of Byzantium from Greek Collections
Why we're looking to Byzantium for decorating inspiration for Christmas and beyond
Holy Chic: Byzantine Glory in Art and Fashion at the Met

architecture.markers: Centralized cross-in-square or domed basilica plans, large domes on pendentives with ringed windows, clustered semi-domes, round arches, banded brick and stone exteriors.

sources.title: Byzantine (culture and style) (AAT 300020669)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

interior.markers: Domed, centrally planned spaces sheathed in gold-ground mosaics and colored marble revetment; round arches on columns, icons and screens, glinting lamplight on gilt surfaces.

lighting.markers: Polycandela: flat pierced copper-alloy discs with cross motifs hung on chains, holding glass oil lamps; massed in churches, casting patterned shadows across walls and floors

decorative-arts.markers: Compound-twill silks woven with large roundels framing griffins, lions, elephants and other beasts in deep blue, red, buff and white.

fashion.markers: Long T-shaped dalmatic tunics with wide sleeves and clavi stripes, cloaks with jewelled tablion panels, patterned silks, pearl-hung crowns and heavy gold-and-gem jewelry.

fine-art.markers: Frontal, elongated saints on flat gold grounds, large almond eyes, stylized linear drapery, halos, inverse perspective, tempera on wood panel icons; glittering tesserae mosaics.

styles.name: Romanesque
styles.description: Medieval European style (c. 1000–1150): massive masonry walls, semicircular arches, barrel and groin vaults, sturdy piers, small windows and a heavy, fortress-like solidity.

sources.title: A journey through Romanesque architecture in Portugal: Interview with spaceworkers

architecture.markers: Massive thick masonry walls, semicircular arches and arcades, small round-headed windows, barrel and groin vaults, sturdy towers, blind arcading and sculpted portal tympana.

sources.title: Romanesque (AAT 300020768)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

decorative-arts.markers: Gilt-copper plaques, crosses and reliquaries in champlevé and cloisonné enamel; stylised frontal figures framed by enamel borders in blue, green and white.

fine-art.markers: Carved portal tympana with Christ in Majesty, stiff stylized figures sized by importance, interlace and monster capitals; flat frescoes and manuscripts with bold outlines.

variants.name: Mosan
variants.description: Romanesque art of the Meuse valley (11th–13th c., present-day Belgium): gilt-copper metalwork and champlevé enamel of classicising figures and refined iconography.
variants.markers: Gilt copper-alloy plaques and reliquaries in champlevé and cloisonné enamel; classicising figures; off-white, mid-green and blue enamel frames.

sources.title: Mosan (AAT 300264268)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

styles.name: Richardsonian Romanesque
styles.description: Late-19th-century American Romanesque Revival named for H. H. Richardson: rough-faced stone, broad round arches, squat columns, deep-set windows, towers and heavy massing.

sources.title: Romanesque Revival - Richardsonian Romanesque (Colorado Historic Architecture & Engineering Guide)

architecture.markers: Rough-faced rusticated stone, broad low round arches over deep-set entrances, squat columns, round towers with conical roofs, ribbon windows, heavy horizontal massing.

sources.title: Richardsonian Romanesque (AAT 300018212)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

styles.name: Gothic
styles.description: Medieval European style (c. 1140–1500): pointed arches, ribbed vaults, flying buttresses, tracery and stained glass; its imagery of ruins, spires and shadow later shaped Gothic horror in fiction and film.

sources.title: Design for Film: The Hollywood Art Director (press release, 1978)
Gothic Architecture: Everything You Need to Know

architecture.markers: Pointed arches, ribbed vaults, flying buttresses, soaring spires and pinnacles, large stained-glass windows with tracery, rose windows, sculpted portals and pronounced verticality.

sources.title: Gothic (Medieval) (AAT 300020775)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

sources.title: Gothic Architecture: Everything You Need to Know

interior.markers: Soaring ribbed vaults on clustered piers, pointed arches, traceried stained-glass windows casting colored light, carved stone and oak screens, choir stalls and tiled floors.

sources.title: E29: English Roman Catholic Church in the Gothic Style, 1275–1300
Gothic Architecture: Everything You Need to Know

furniture.markers: Joined oak chests carved with tracery, pointed arches and figures, iron strapwork, choir-stall-like chairs, trestle tables, canopied beds; architecture at human scale.

sources.title: Everything to know about Gothic and Renaissance furniture

lighting.markers: Interior flooded with colored light from tall lancet and rose windows of deep blue and ruby stained glass set in lead and stone tracery; light treated as divine radiance

sources.title: English and French Medieval Stained Glass in the Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

decorative-arts.markers: Pointed arches, tracery and rose-window geometry; jewel-toned stained glass with narrative figures in lead lines; elegant swaying figures; micro-architecture on metalwork.

media_markers.arms-and-armor: Late-15th-c. plate with slender pointed forms, sharp ridges and grooves echoing tracery, cusped edges, sallet helmets with long tails and pointed sabatons.

fashion.markers: Voluminous belted houppelande gowns with dagged edges, parti-colored hose, poulaines with long pointed toes, chaperon hoods and tall headdresses.

fine-art.markers: Gold-ground altarpieces and polyptychs in pointed-arch frames, elongated swaying S-curve figures, flowing drapery, jewel-like color; cathedral jamb statues and carved portals.

film.markers: Studio castles, crypts and ruined abbeys with pointed arches and cobwebbed stone stairs; candlelight and deep shadow; fog-bound graveyards; capes; lurid Technicolor blood (Hammer).

sources.title: Design for Film: The Hollywood Art Director (press release, 1978)
Gothic: The Dark Heart of British Film (touring programme)

variants.name: Decorated Gothic
variants.description: Middle phase of English Gothic (c. 1290–1350), named by Thomas Rickman: large windows with geometric then flowing curvilinear tracery and lavish carved ornament.
variants.markers: Large windows with geometric or flowing curvilinear tracery, ogee arches, ballflower and naturalistic foliage carving, crocketed pinnacles and gables.

sources.title: Decorated Style (AAT 300020799)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

variants.name: Early English
variants.description: First phase of English Gothic (c. 1180–1275), named by Thomas Rickman: pointed arches, tall narrow lancet windows and a long, low silhouette, as at Salisbury Cathedral.
variants.markers: Tall narrow lancet windows singly or in groups, pointed arches, slender dark marble shafts, steep gables, long low silhouette with a spire, stiff-leaf carving, little tracery.

sources.title: Early English (AAT 300020796)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

variants.name: Isabelline
variants.description: Late Gothic style of Spain under Isabella I (c. 1480–1510), combining Flemish Gothic and Mudéjar elements with heraldic display.
variants.markers: Façades encrusted with carved heraldry and coats of arms, star vaults, stalactite cornices, beaded ornament, ogee and multifoil arches, lacy openwork.

sources.title: Isabelline (AAT 300021133)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

variants.name: Rayonnant
variants.description: Middle phase of French Gothic (c. 1240–1350) radiating from Paris: lighter structures with walls dissolved into glass and tracery, and great rose windows.
variants.markers: Walls dissolved into stained glass and bar tracery, huge radiating rose windows, glazed triforium, slender mullions, sharp gables over portals, delicate pinnacles.

sources.title: Rayonnant (AAT 300020859)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

styles.name: Gothic Revival
styles.description: 18th–19th-century revival of medieval Gothic forms: pointed arches, steep gables, tracery, pinnacles and carved ornament in churches, houses, interiors and furniture.

sources.title: Gothic Revival (Colorado Historic Architecture & Engineering Guide)

architecture.markers: Steep cross gables, pointed-arch windows with tracery, decorative bargeboards, pinnacles and finials, towers and battlements, board-and-batten or masonry walls.

sources.title: Gothic Revival Architecture: Origins, Features & Legacy
Gothic Revival (AAT 300021452)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

interior.markers: Pointed-arch doors and windows, traceried oak paneling, ribbed or beamed ceilings, encaustic tiles, heraldic patterned wallpapers in deep reds and greens, carved oak furniture with finials.

sources.title: Gothic Revival Style 1830 - 1860 | PHMC > Pennsylvania Architectural Field Guide
A Gothic Revival House in the English Countryside

furniture.markers: Pointed-arch tracery backs and panels, crockets, pinnacles, quatrefoils and cusped arcading; dark oak or walnut; church-like hall chairs, cabinets and sideboards.

sources.title: Armchair, A.W.N. Pugin for Scarisbrick Hall, 1837-40
Art: A Matter of Style: Gothic Revival

lighting.markers: Brass coronae and gasoliers in medieval forms; hexagonal glazed lanterns with saw-pierced bands on leafy scrolled brackets (Pugin, Skidmore)

sources.title: Sketch designs for a corona, A.W.N. Pugin
Design for a bracket and lantern, A.W.N. Pugin

decorative-arts.markers: Flat, conventionalised medieval ornament: heraldic devices, fleurs-de-lis, quatrefoils and tracery in deep reds, blues and gold; revived medieval-style stained-glass figures.

media_markers.wallcoverings: Pugin papers with flat heraldic and Gothic diaper repeats rejecting illusionistic depth; strong reds, greens and gold.

sources.title: Stained glass: the Gothic Revival and beyond
Wallpaper, A.W.N. Pugin, The Grange, Ramsgate (Style: Gothic Revival)

styles.name: Carpenter Gothic
styles.description: North American wood-frame Gothic Revival: board-and-batten siding, steep gables, pointed-arch windows and jigsaw-cut gingerbread bargeboards made with scroll saws.

architecture.markers: Wooden houses and churches with steep gables, lacy scroll-sawn bargeboards and trim, pointed-arch windows, board-and-batten siding and finials.

sources.title: Carpenter Gothic (AAT 300107913)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

styles.name: Renaissance
styles.description: 15th–16th-century European style rooted in Italy that revived classical antiquity: harmonious proportion, symmetry, columns, pilasters, round arches and hemispherical domes.

sources.title: Kings, Queens, and Courtiers: Art in Early Renaissance France
Kings, Queens, and Courtiers: Art in Early Renaissance France
Renaissance Architecture: Everything You Need to Know About This Classic European Style

architecture.markers: Symmetrical façades ordered by classical pilasters and columns, round arches, rusticated ground floors, regular rows of pedimented windows, heavy cornices, domes on drums.

sources.title: Renaissance (AAT 300021140)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

sources.title: Renaissance Architecture: Everything You Need to Know About This Classic European Style

interior.markers: Ordered, proportioned rooms with coffered or painted beamed ceilings, classical pilasters and doorcases, intarsia paneling, tapestries, marble or terracotta floors, carved walnut chests and chairs.

sources.title: Studiolo from the Ducal Palace in Gubbio
At the Heart of the Renaissance Palace - The Salle des Caryatides
E17: French Bedroom of the Henri IV Period, Late 16th Century
Renaissance Architecture: Everything You Need to Know About This Classic European Style

furniture.markers: Carved walnut with classical columns, grotesques, acanthus and scrolls; cassoni, credenzas, X-frame chairs, intarsia and gilded or painted panels.

sources.title: Everything to know about Gothic and Renaissance furniture

decorative-arts.markers: Classical ornament revived: grotesques, acanthus, trophies and medallions; narrative painted scenes; rich silk velvets; etched and embossed parade armour.

media_markers.ceramics: Italian tin-glazed maiolica in cobalt, ochre, green and manganese; istoriato plates covered edge to edge with mythological or biblical scenes.
media_markers.arms-and-armor: Etched and gilt bands of foliage; embossed all'antica parade armour; steel imitating puffed-and-slashed civilian dress.

sources.title: Five armoured lames, Konrad Seusenhofer, ca. 1515 (Style: Renaissance)

fashion.markers: Layered Italian gowns (gamurra, giornea) of velvet and brocaded silk, detachable sleeves, dark luxurious menswear; colorful double-sided enamelled pendant jewels.

fine-art.markers: Linear perspective, balanced pyramidal compositions, naturalistic anatomy, sfumato and chiaroscuro modeling, classical architecture backdrops; contrapposto marble and bronze figures.

variants.name: Herrerian
variants.description: Austere Spanish Renaissance style of the late 16th–17th c., named after Juan de Herrera and epitomized by El Escorial.
variants.markers: Severe granite blocks with almost no ornament, rigid symmetry, corner towers with slate spires, pyramid-and-ball finials, plain classical orders, grids of windows.

sources.title: Herreran (AAT 300021135)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

variants.name: Louis XIII
variants.description: French style under Louis XIII (1610–1643), between Renaissance and Baroque: ebony-veneered cabinets, turned and twist-turned supports, geometric panels and Renaissance-derived classical ornament.
variants.markers: Ebony-veneered cabinets on stands with carved figural panels; spiral- and bobbin-turned legs with H-stretchers; square-backed upholstered chairs; geometric moldings.

variants.name: Venetian School
variants.description: Painting of Renaissance Venice from the late 1400s (Bellini, Giorgione, Titian, Tintoretto, Veronese), prizing color and light over drawn contour.
variants.markers: Rich glowing color, warm golden light, soft atmospheric landscapes, loose visible brushwork in late works, sumptuous fabrics, reclining nudes and grand banquet scenes.

variants.name: Maximilian
variants.description: German plate-armour fashion of c. 1500–1540, named for Emperor Maximilian I: closely set parallel fluting over most surfaces, rounded forms and broad 'bear-paw' sabatons.
variants.markers: Steel plates covered with dense parallel flutes; rounded breastplates; close helmets with fluted skulls; broad, blunt-toed sabatons.

styles.name: Mannerism
styles.description: Late-Renaissance style (c. 1520–1600) that deliberately distorted classical rules: elongated proportions, unexpected juxtapositions, broken pediments and visual tension.

architecture.markers: Classical elements used against the rules: broken or slipped pediments, keystones dropping, exaggerated rustication, blind niches, elongated proportions and tense, ambiguous façades.

sources.title: Mannerist (Renaissance-Baroque style) (AAT 300021144)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

fine-art.markers: Elongated limbs and necks, twisting serpentine poses, crowded ambiguous space, acid and shot colors, cool polished surfaces and artificial, self-conscious elegance.

styles.name: Renaissance Revival
styles.description: 19th-century revival of Italian and French Renaissance forms in buildings and furniture: rusticated bases, arched windows, pediments, and heavy carved walnut case pieces.

sources.title: Renaissance Revival (Colorado Historic Architecture & Engineering Guide)

architecture.markers: Symmetrical block with low hipped tile roof, wide bracketed eaves, arched ground-floor openings and loggias, rusticated base, classical window surrounds and string courses.

sources.title: Renaissance Revival (AAT 300021464)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

furniture.markers: Massive architectural case pieces with broken pediments, applied medallions and plaques, acorn trim, baluster-turned legs; walnut and burl veneer, carved busts and cartouches.

sources.title: Art: A Matter of Style: Renaissance Revival
Collecting guide: key periods of American furniture

styles.name: Baroque
styles.description: 17th–early-18th-century European style of drama and grandeur: dynamic curves, rich materials, gilding, illusionistic ceilings, monumental scale and theatrical light.

architecture.markers: Dynamic curving and convex-concave façades, giant orders, broken pediments, layered columns, oval domes and lanterns, dramatic sculpture and theatrical light and shadow.

media_markers.urban: Towns planned for theatrical effect: straight streets and axes ending on church facades, scenographic piazzas, monumental stairways and unified honey-stone street fronts.

sources.title: Baroque (AAT 300021147)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

sources.title: Late Baroque Towns of the Val di Noto (South-Eastern Sicily)
Baroque Architecture: Everything You Need to Know

interior.markers: Monumental symmetrical state rooms in enfilade: illusionistic painted ceilings, gilded stucco and carved giltwood, marble walls and floors, velvet and damask hangings, mirrors and dramatic light.

sources.title: Baroque Architecture: Everything You Need to Know

furniture.markers: Sculptural carved and gilded frames, heavy scrolls and acanthus, pietra dura and marquetry, twist-turned legs, massive cabinets on stands, rich velvet upholstery.

sources.title: The A-Z guide to antique furniture

lighting.markers: Chased gilt-bronze chandeliers with baluster shaft, flame finial, scrolling branches, dolphins and lion masks; Venetian clear-glass chandeliers ornamented with coloured glass flowers

decorative-arts.markers: Heavy, sculptural silver and silver-gilt; exotic porcelain, lacquer and shell set in lavish mounts; dense naturalistic and figural ornament.

media_markers.musical-instruments: Flemish harpsichords and virginals with block-printed arabesque papers on cases, soundboards painted with flowers, and marbled exteriors.

fashion.markers: Falling lace collars, satin doublets, love-locks and long curled hair, later cascading full-bottomed wigs, lace cravats and billowing drapery.

fine-art.markers: Dramatic diagonals, strong chiaroscuro and theatrical spotlighting, swirling drapery, intense emotion and movement, illusionistic ceiling frescoes, dynamic marble figure groups.

variants.name: Restoration
variants.description: English style from the restoration of Charles II (1660) to 1688: opulent Baroque forms influenced by Holland and France, walnut, caning, lacquer and exotic imports.
variants.markers: Tall caned-back walnut chairs with carved crests, spiral-twist turned legs and stretchers, scrolled feet, floral marquetry, lacquer cabinets on carved stands.

variants.name: Quito School
variants.description: Colonial school of religious painting and polychrome sculpture in Quito, Ecuador (founded 1552, flourishing in the 17th–18th c.), known for gilded, finely painted wooden saints and gold-leaf church interiors.
variants.markers: Small polychrome wood figures with estofado gilding under painted robes, glass eyes, silver halos, porcelain-smooth flesh tones; winged Virgin of Quito standing on a crescent and serpent.

sources.title: Quito (AAT 300107841)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

sources.title: Virgin of Quito
sources.publisher: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Collection API)

variants.name: Brazilian Baroque
variants.description: Baroque and Rococo of colonial Brazil (18th c.), above all in the gold-mining towns of Minas Gerais (Ouro Preto, Congonhas), with churches and statuary by Aleijadinho carved in local soapstone.
variants.markers: Whitewashed churches with curved façades, round twin towers, soapstone portals carved with medallions, scrolls and angels, framed in grey-green stone pilasters.

sources.title: LISBOA ANTONIO FRANCISCO, dit ALEIJADINHO (1738 env.-1814)

variants.name: Hispano-Philippine
variants.description: Ivory devotional sculpture carved in the Spanish Philippines, chiefly Manila (late 16th–19th c.), after European and Asian models, and exported to Latin America.
variants.markers: Ivory figures of the Virgin, Christ and saints after European prototypes, with Asian-inflected faces.

sources.title: Hispano-Philippine (AAT 300448849)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

styles.name: Louis XIV
styles.description: French Baroque court style (c. 1643–1715) epitomized by Versailles: massive symmetrical furniture, gilt bronze, Boulle marquetry, carved giltwood and regal grandeur.

sources.title: Furnishings during the Reign of Louis XIV (1654-1715)
Louis XIV Decor and Spring Roses: Inside the Restoration of an 18th-Century French Château

architecture.markers: French Baroque classicism: long symmetrical palace façades with giant orders, rusticated base, balustraded flat rooflines with trophies and urns, avant-corps, formal axial layout.

sources.title: Louis XIV (AAT 300021080)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

interior.markers: Grand symmetrical salons with marble or parquet floors, gilded carved paneling, painted and gilded ceilings, mirrors, tapestries, Boulle-marquetry cabinets and massive giltwood furniture on axis.

sources.title: E18: French Salon of the Louis XIV Period, 1660–1700
E19: French Dining Room of the Louis XIV Period, 1660–1700
Sun and Gold - The Galerie d’Apollon

furniture.markers: Massive symmetrical forms; Boulle marquetry of brass and tortoiseshell; gilt-bronze mounts; carved giltwood consoles; baluster or scrolled legs joined by X- or H-stretchers.

lighting.markers: Gilt-bronze chandeliers with diving dolphins and flame finials; mirrored galleries lit by thousands of candles on chandeliers and torchères with girandoles

fashion.markers: Knee-length justaucorps coats with deep cuffs over waistcoat and breeches, periwigs, heeled shoes; women's mantua gowns and tall wired fontange headdresses.

styles.name: Rococo
styles.description: 18th-century style born in France: asymmetry, shell and scroll (rocaille) motifs, pastel colors, gilded stucco and lighter, more intimate and playful interiors than Baroque.

sources.title: Rococo: The Continuing Curve, 1730-2008 by Sarah D. Coffin, Gail Davidson, Ellen Lupton , Penelope Hunter-Stiebel

architecture.markers: Pastel-washed stucco façades, curved bays and oval domed salons, playful sculpted herms and rocaille cartouches around tall French windows, low single-storey pleasure pavilions.

sources.title: Rococo (AAT 300021155)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

interior.markers: Intimate salons of white-and-gold carved boiseries with asymmetric rocaille shells and C-scrolls, pastel silks, mirrored overmantels, painted overdoors and curvaceous upholstered seating.

sources.title: Boiserie from the Hôtel de Varengeville

furniture.markers: Asymmetric C- and S-scroll and shell (rocaille) carving, serpentine and bombé fronts, cabriole legs, gilt-bronze mounts, gilded or pastel-painted frames, floral marquetry.

sources.title: The A-Z guide to antique furniture

lighting.markers: Asymmetric giltwood girandoles and candlestands carved with scrolls, shells, trees, dolphins and stalactites; porcelain wall lights with gilt-bronze tulip candle holders

sources.title: Chandeliers de Sculpture en Argent, ca.1745

decorative-arts.markers: Asymmetric rocaille shells, C- and S-scrolls, marine motifs and naturalistic flowers; porcelain vases and figures; silver with chased scrolls; pastel grounds with gilding.

media_markers.textiles: Printed calicoes with meandering naturalistic flowers and trailing stems on light grounds.
media_markers.musical-instruments: Harpsichord soundboards painted with flowers, insects and birds around a cast rose.

sources.title: Rococo textile designs by William Kilburn

fashion.markers: Robe à la française with back box pleats, wide panniers, decorated stomachers, pastel floral silks, ruffled sleeves, bows, lace, fans.

fine-art.markers: Pastel pinks and blues, feathery brushwork, fêtes galantes in parkland, flirtatious aristocrats, swings, putti and garlands, intimate scale and playful erotic charm.

variants.name: Régence
variants.description: French style of c. 1700–1730, including the regency of Philippe d'Orléans (1715–1723), bridging Louis XIV formality and Rococo with lighter curves, early rocaille, grotesques and chinoiserie.
variants.markers: Early cabriole legs, bombé commodes with sculptural gilt-bronze mounts, symmetrical shell and lambrequin ornament, bois satiné and amaranth veneers, parquetry.

sources.title: The A-Z guide to antique furniture

styles.name: Louis XV
styles.description: French Rococo furniture and interiors (c. 1730–1760): cabriole legs, serpentine fronts, naturalistic carving, marquetry, comfortable upholstered seating and gilt mounts.

sources.title: A Royal Taste: Louis XV-1738, Metropolitan Museum Journal v. 7
E21: French Boudoir of the Louis XV Period, 1740–60

interior.markers: Smaller, comfortable rooms with curving carved boiseries in white, gold or pastel, overmantel mirrors, rocaille ornament, cabriole-legged bergères, marquetry commodes and silk upholstery.

sources.title: E21: French Boudoir of the Louis XV Period, 1740–60
Boiserie from the Hôtel de Varengeville
A Royal Taste: Louis XV—1738 (Metropolitan Museum Journal, v. 7)

styles.name: Insular Art

styles.name: International Gothic
styles.description: Courtly late-Gothic style that spread across Europe c. 1375–1425: refined, decorative, richly colored art with elegant figures and naturalistic detail.

fine-art.markers: Elegant swaying figures in flowing robes, rich gold and ultramarine, tooled gold grounds, courtly costume, minute flowers and animals, flattened decorative space.

styles.name: International Typographic Style
styles.description: Swiss-led graphic design style (c. 1950–1970) built on modular grids, asymmetric layouts, sans-serif type, objective photography and zero ornament for clear, rational communication. Also called Swiss Style.

variants.name: New Typography
variants.description: Modernist typographic doctrine (1920s–1930s) codified by Jan Tschichold's Die neue Typographie (1928): asymmetric, functional layouts in sans-serif type with rules, photography and limited colour.
variants.markers: Asymmetric layouts, sans-serif type, bold rules and bars, functional hierarchy, photography over drawing, two-colour printing (black with red or blue).

styles.name: Islamic

styles.name: Noh

styles.name: Orientalism

fine-art.markers: Densely patterned flat figurative compositions of Yoruba deities, spirits and folk tales; hybrid magical creatures; intricate line infill; linocuts, paintings and beaded or appliqué panels.

styles.name: Kinshasa Popular Painting
styles.description: Urban figurative painting movement founded in mid-1970s Kinshasa by largely self-taught artists (Chéri Samba, Moke, Chéri Chérin, Bodo) rooted in sign and billboard painting.

sources.title: Earring (one of a pair), Silla Kingdom

fashion.markers: Hollow sheet-gold earrings with granulation and dangling leaf-shaped spangles; gold crowns with tree and antler uprights; strings of glass and comma-shaped (gogok) beads.

sources.title: Earring (one of a pair), Silla Kingdom

fine-art.markers: Small gilt-bronze standing and seated Buddhas with calm faces, rounded bodies and clinging robes; granite tomb panels carved with zodiac figures in armour.

styles.name: Minhwa
styles.description: Korean folk painting of the late Joseon period (18th–early 20th c.), used in palaces and ordinary homes: auspicious tigers and magpies, flowers and birds, books and longevity symbols.

fine-art.markers: Bright mineral colours and flat bold forms: humorous striped tigers with magpies in pines, paired birds amid peonies, cranes and pines, book-shelf screens; folding-screen formats.

styles.name: Zanabazar School
styles.description: Mongolian Buddhist sculpture of Zanabazar (1635–1723), first Jebtsundamba Khutughtu, and his followers: Nepalese-derived gilt-bronze deities of youthful grace.

sources.title: Fine Arts Museum, Ulaanbaatar: Zanabazar and his school
sources.publisher: University of Washington, Silk Road Seattle

sources.title: Introduction to the Art of Mongolia (Terese Tse Bartholomew)

fine-art.markers: Seamless gilt-bronze Taras and Buddhas: slender youthful bodies, high foreheads, arched brows, small full lips, long bead strands across the torso; double-lotus bases.

sources.title: Fine Arts Museum, Ulaanbaatar: Zanabazar and his school
sources.publisher: University of Washington, Silk Road Seattle

sources.title: Introduction to the Art of Mongolia (Terese Tse Bartholomew)

styles.name: Taiwan New Cinema
styles.description: Taiwanese film movement of the 1980s–90s (Hou Hsiao-hsien, Edward Yang): restrained social realism about ordinary lives amid urbanization and Taiwan's history.

sources.title: The many voices behind Taiwan New Cinema
A guide to Taiwan's dreamy New Cinema movement

film.markers: Long takes and static distant framing; natural light and real locations; layered compositions through doorways and windows; quiet domestic, rural and Taipei street life.

sources.title: A guide to Taiwan's dreamy New Cinema movement

styles.name: Sumerian
styles.description: Art and architecture of Sumer in southern Mesopotamia (c. 3500–2000 BCE): mud-brick temples and ziggurats, wide-eyed votive statues, cylinder seals, and gold, lapis and carnelian regalia from the Royal Cemetery at Ur.

sources.title: Art of the First Cities in the Third Millennium B.C.
Mesopotamian art and architecture - Sumerian period
Sumerian
sources.publisher: Fashion History Timeline (Fashion Institute of Technology)

architecture.markers: Stepped mud-brick ziggurats with ramp stairways, baked-brick facing panelled with buttresses and recesses, temple platforms in walled precincts.

sources.title: Art of the First Cities in the Third Millennium B.C.

fashion.markers: Gold leaf-and-ring headdresses, wreaths of beech and willow leaves, lapis lazuli and carnelian bead collars, huge crescent earrings, fringed fleece skirts.

fine-art.markers: Gypsum or limestone votive figures standing with hands clasped, huge inlaid shell-and-lapis eyes, fleece kaunakes skirts; shell-inlaid narrative panels and cylinder seals.

sources.title: Mesopotamian art and architecture - Sculpture, Reliefs, Statues
Art of the First Cities in the Third Millennium B.C.

styles.name: Assyrian
styles.description: Art of the Assyrian empire of northern Mesopotamia (c. 1365–609 BCE), above all the Neo-Assyrian palaces of Nimrud, Khorsabad and Nineveh with gateway colossi and narrative stone reliefs.

sources.title: Assyrian
sources.publisher: Fashion History Timeline (Fashion Institute of Technology)

architecture.markers: Mud-brick palace citadels on raised platforms; gateways flanked by colossal human-headed winged bulls (lamassu); rooms lined with carved gypsum orthostat slabs.

fine-art.markers: Low-relief gypsum panels of royal lion hunts, sieges and tribute processions; profile figures with curled beards and fringed robes; winged genies; cuneiform text bands.

styles.name: Neo-Babylonian
styles.description: Art and architecture of the Neo-Babylonian empire (626–539 BCE), centred on Nebuchadnezzar II's rebuilt Babylon: monumental gates and processional ways faced in molded, colored glazed brick.

architecture.markers: Crenellated gates and walls faced in deep blue glazed brick with molded striding lions, bulls and mushhushshu dragons in yellow and white; rosette friezes; ziggurat Etemenanki.

styles.name: Hittite
styles.description: Art of the Hittites of Anatolia (c. 1650–1180 BCE), centred on Hattusa: cyclopean stone fortifications, rock-carved reliefs of gods, and animal-form vessels in clay and precious metal.

architecture.markers: Massive cyclopean stone walls with corbelled-arch gates guarded by carved lions or sphinxes; postern tunnels; temple courtyards; open-air rock sanctuaries.

decorative-arts.markers: Burnished red clay beak-spouted jugs, bull-shaped libation vessels and stag- or fist-shaped silver rhyta with relief friezes.

fine-art.markers: Rock-cut reliefs of processing deities in tall pointed horned caps, short kilts and upturned shoes; heavy stocky figures; hieroglyphic Luwian signs.

styles.name: Phoenician
styles.description: Art of the Phoenician city-states of the Levant coast (c. 1500–300 BCE), an eclectic blend of Egyptian, Assyrian, Aegean and Syrian motifs spread by trade: carved ivories, metal bowls and glass.

decorative-arts.markers: Carved ivory furniture plaques with sphinxes, griffins, lotus and palmettes, 'woman at the window'; gilt silver bowls with concentric friezes; core-formed glass.

styles.name: Achaemenid
styles.description: Court art of the Achaemenid Persian empire (c. 550–330 BCE), as at Persepolis and Susa: columned audience halls, processional stone reliefs and gold vessels uniting Mesopotamian, Egyptian and Greek forms.

architecture.markers: Raised terraces with double ramp stairs; hypostyle halls (apadana) of tall slender fluted columns crowned by back-to-back bull or griffin protome capitals; glazed-brick archers.

decorative-arts.markers: Gold and silver rhyta ending in lion or griffin foreparts, fluted phialai, griffin-headed armlets, inlaid gold plaques.

fine-art.markers: Stone staircase reliefs of tribute bearers and guards in long processional rows, crisp folded robes, curled beards, lion-and-bull combat, winged disc emblem.

styles.name: Parthian
styles.description: Art of the Parthian empire in Iran and Mesopotamia (247 BCE–224 CE), mixing Hellenistic and Iranian traditions; known for the iwan, stucco decoration and strictly frontal figures.

architecture.markers: Barrel-vaulted iwan halls open to courtyards, ashlar or brick façades with engaged columns and carved stucco or stone masks and friezes, as at Hatra.

fine-art.markers: Rigidly frontal statues and reliefs of rulers in belted tunics, baggy trousers and diadems, staring eyes, linear drapery folds.

styles.name: Sasanian
styles.description: Art of the Sasanian empire of Iran (224–651 CE): royal rock reliefs, gilded silver hunting plates, stucco, roundel silks and vast brick vaults, a key source for early Islamic art.

architecture.markers: Huge parabolic brick vaults and iwans (Taq-i Kisra), domes on squinches over square halls, rubble-and-mortar fire temples, blind-arcaded façades.

decorative-arts.markers: Gilded silver plates of the king hunting on horseback; silks with pearl-bordered roundels of senmurvs, boars and rams; carved stucco panels.

fine-art.markers: Monumental cliff reliefs of investitures, triumphs over Roman emperors and equestrian jousts; kings with crenellated crowns, globe finials and fluttering ribbons.

styles.name: Nabataean
styles.description: Art of the Nabataean Arab kingdom (c. 4th century BCE–106 CE), centred on Petra: rock-cut tomb and temple façades blending Hellenistic, Egyptian and Mesopotamian elements, and eggshell-thin painted pottery.

architecture.markers: Temple and tomb façades carved into rose-red sandstone cliffs: two-storey columned fronts, broken pediments, tholos centrepieces, crow-step merlons, horned capitals.

decorative-arts.markers: Eggshell-thin wheel-made bowls painted in dark red-brown with dense palmettes, leaves and feathered motifs on a pinkish ground.

styles.name: Coptic
styles.description: Art of Christian Egypt (c. 4th–12th centuries, chiefly 300–800 CE): bright, flat colour, static frontal figures and Syrian, Near Eastern and pharaonic motifs in textiles, carvings, wall paintings and churches.

sources.title: Coptic Art, Dikran Kelekian, and Milton Avery

decorative-arts.markers: Linen tunics with tapestry-woven purple and red wool roundels, clavi bands and squares; vine scrolls, interlace, dancers, saints and busts with large eyes.

sources.title: Textile Fragment (slit tapestry with Coptic inscription, Egypt, ca. 600–800)

fine-art.markers: Flat, frontal saints and monks with oversized eyes and heavy outlines on bright grounds; deeply drilled limestone reliefs of vines, acanthus and mythological figures.

sources.title: Coptic Art, Dikran Kelekian, and Milton Avery

styles.name: Sogdian
styles.description: Art of pre-Islamic Sogdiana in Central Asia (5th–9th centuries), as at Panjikent: narrative wall paintings, carved wood and silver blending Sasanian, Indian and Chinese sources.

fine-art.markers: Wall paintings in horizontal registers of epic heroes, banquets and deities; slender figures in patterned kaftans on red or ultramarine grounds; carved wood friezes.

styles.name: Hurufiyya
styles.description: Modern art movement in the Arab world and wider Islamic world (from the 1950s) using Arabic letters as abstract compositional elements, distinct from classical calligraphy.

sources.title: Barjeel Art Foundation presents Hurufiyya: Art & Identity at Bibliotheca Alexandrina
Collection Highlight: Madiha Umar, Precursor of Early Modern Calligraphy
sources.publisher: Qatar Museums (Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art)

fine-art.markers: Arabic letterforms deconstructed, overlaid and enlarged into abstract compositions; swirling script rhythms, calligraphic gesture, textured grounds.

sources.title: Collection Highlight: Madiha Umar, Precursor of Early Modern Calligraphy
sources.publisher: Qatar Museums (Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art)

sources.title: Barjeel Art Foundation presents Hurufiyya: Art & Identity at Bibliotheca Alexandrina

styles.name: Saqqakhaneh
styles.description: Neo-traditional Iranian modernist movement (late 1950s–1960s) drawing on Shi'ite votive art, folk art, calligraphy and pre-Islamic motifs; the term was coined by critic Karim Emami in 1963.

sources.title: Azari 2021 exhibitions (Spiritual Pop: Art in 1960s Iran)
Asia Society Museum Announces 26 Artists to Participate in First Major Exhibition of Modern Art from Iran

fine-art.markers: Votive Shi'ite motifs, talismans, open hands and padlocks, calligraphy, seals and folk patterns in flat bright colour; bronze sculptures of letterforms.

sources.title: Asia Society Museum Announces 26 Artists to Participate in First Major Exhibition of Modern Art from Iran

styles.name: Baghdad Modern Art Group
styles.description: Iraqi modernist group founded in 1951 by Jewad Selim and Shakir Hassan Al Said, interpreting Western abstraction through Islamic and Mesopotamian heritage (istilham al-turath).

sources.title: First Comprehensive Survey of The Baghdad Modern Art Group Opens June 2025 at CCS Bard's Hessel Museum of Art

fine-art.markers: Flattened, stylized figures and crescent, eye and Mesopotamian motifs; abstraction drawing on Islamic geometry, manuscript painting and Arabic script.

sources.title: First Comprehensive Survey of The Baghdad Modern Art Group Opens June 2025 at CCS Bard's Hessel Museum of Art

styles.name: Iranian New Wave
styles.description: Iranian film movement emerging in the late 1960s and flourishing after 1979 (Kiarostami, Mehrjui, Makhmalbaf): poetic realism, observational storytelling and reflexive, philosophical narratives.

sources.title: MoMA and P.S.1 present first major United States retrospective of Abbas Kiarostami (press release)
Friendly Persuasion: Iranian Cinema After the Revolution

film.markers: Long static takes, nonprofessional and child actors, dusty rural roads and hills in wide shots, car-interior dialogue, natural light, blurred fiction and documentary.

sources.title: MoMA and P.S.1 present first major United States retrospective of Abbas Kiarostami (press release)
Abbas Kiarostami's Early Shorts and Features: Poetic Solutions to Philosophical Problems

styles.name: Bezalel School

sources.title: Modern Ritual: From Bezalel to Wolpert
sources.publisher: Derfner Judaica Museum via Google Arts & Culture

sources.publisher: Derfner Judaica Museum via Google Arts & Culture

styles.name: Najdi
styles.description: Architectural and decorative style of central Arabia (Najd), exemplified by the 18th-century palaces of at-Turaif in ad-Dir'iyah: adobe construction adapted to extreme desert climate.

architecture.markers: Thick mud-brick walls with crenellated parapets, high triangular ventilation openings, plastered lime-washed stone columns and capitals, keel arches, tall towers.

styles.name: Amazigh (Berber)

styles.name: Gandhara

styles.name: Mathura

styles.name: Chola

styles.name: Hoysala
styles.description: Temple architecture and sculpture of the Hoysala dynasty of Karnataka (12th–13th centuries), as at Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura, noted for intricately carved soapstone.

sources.title: Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas - UNESCO World Heritage Centre
Hoysala (AAT 300018916)
sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

architecture.markers: Star-shaped plans on high jagati platforms, low stepped towers, wall bands of elephant, horse and scroll friezes, lathe-turned soapstone pillars, bracket maidens.

fine-art.markers: Dark chloritic schist deities carved in lace-like depth: tall jewelled crowns, dense pendant ornaments, foliate arches overhead, small attendant figures at the feet.

styles.name: Indo-Islamic

sources.title: South Asian arts - Indian Architecture, Temples, Mosques

styles.name: Deccani

fine-art.markers: Elongated figures, high horizons, floral-sprigged grounds, lavish gold, rich lilac and green palettes, dreamlike composite animals, gold-sprinkled borders.

techniques.name: Limewash
techniques.description: Paint of slaked lime and water, plain white or tinted with earth pigments, that soaks into masonry, render or wood and cures by carbonation into a breathable mineral coat.

sources.title: Limewash: An Old Practice and a Good One (U.S. National Park Service) Lock

techniques.markers: Flat, chalky mineral coat with a soft crystalline glow; mottled color that lightens or darkens with the porosity of the wall; bright white or earth tints of cream, yellow and brown.

architecture.markers: Exterior masonry, brick and render walls in bright opaque white or earth tints, slightly uneven, with texture of the wall showing through.

sources.title: Limewash: An Old Practice and a Good One (U.S. National Park Service) Lock

interior.markers: Wall finish on lime-rendered walls with a gently textured, mottled color that deepens and lightens across the surface.

techniques.name: Marquetry
techniques.description: Decorative technique in which small, specially shaped pieces of wood veneer, sometimes with ivory, shell or other materials, are assembled so that the entire surface is veneered, forming a picture or design.
techniques.markers: Flat, sanded surface entirely covered in fitted wood veneers of differing colors and grain directions forming a picture or pattern, with near-invisible joins under a sealing finish.

furniture.markers: Cabinet doors and table tops with large flat areas covered in marquetry flower bouquets or geometric patterns, framed by relatively small mouldings.

fine-art.markers: Pictures assembled from wood veneers and mounted on a backboard, sanded smooth and finished with oil.

variants.name: Floral marquetry
variants.description: Marquetry depicting flower bouquets, as on late 17th-century Dutch cabinets and tables.
variants.markers: Bouquets of flowers laid in wood veneer across the large flat panels of cabinet doors and table tops.

variants.name: Seaweed marquetry
variants.description: Marquetry composed of symmetrical scrolls.
variants.markers: Symmetrical scrolling designs laid in wood veneer across a flat surface.

variants.name: Parquetry
variants.description: Marquetry composed of geometric patterns.
variants.markers: Geometric patterns, such as stars, formed from fitted wood veneers across a flat surface.

techniques.name: Raku
techniques.description: Low-fired pottery removed from the kiln while still glowing hot; Japanese raku cools in open air, while Western raku is set in combustibles that smoke and reduce it.

sources.title: Naked Raku Technique from Experts Charlie and Linda Riggs

techniques.markers: Crazed glaze with crackle lines stained black by smoke, soot-blackened bare clay, and uneven, mottled color from random reduction.

variants.name: Naked raku
variants.description: Raku in which a thick slip coat cracks during firing so smoke reaches the clay only through the cracks; the slip is removed after cooling.
variants.markers: Pale clay surface covered in a fine web of black crackle lines, with masked areas left solid black.

sources.title: Naked Raku Technique from Experts Charlie and Linda Riggs

techniques.name: Sgraffito
techniques.description: Scratching through a top coat on a hard surface to reveal a contrasting layer beneath; used on tinted plaster walls, on slip- or glaze-coated pottery, and in paint.

sources.title: Background on Sgraffito & Art Nouveau | National Building Arts Center

techniques.markers: Crisp two-tone linear design: scratched lines and cut-back areas exposing a contrasting under-color, slightly recessed into the top layer.

architecture.markers: Facades covered in scratched two-tone plaster: ornamental and graphic decoration, or rows of fine geometric patterns.

sources.title: Background on Sgraffito & Art Nouveau | National Building Arts Center
Background on Sgraffito & Art Nouveau | National Building Arts Center

techniques.name: Shibori
techniques.description: Japanese shaped-resist dyeing in which cloth is bound, stitched, pleated, or folded and clamped before dyeing, so the compressed areas resist the dye.

sources.title: Shibori: The Art of Tie-Dyeing | Kyoto National Museum

techniques.markers: Pale undyed patterns against a dyed ground: small rings and dots, spider-web bursts, water-like ripples or diagonal streaks; sometimes indigo blue and white.

fashion.markers: Kimono patterned over large areas with tied dots, rings and multicolored, sometimes pictorial resist designs.

sources.title: Shibori: The Art of Tie-Dyeing | Kyoto National Museum
Shibori: The Art of Tie-Dyeing | Kyoto National Museum

techniques.name: Tadelakt
techniques.description: Moroccan lime plaster compacted and burnished with a polishing stone, then sealed with olive-oil soap that reacts with the lime to give a water-resistant surface.

sources.title: Tadelakt: What you Need to Know About Moroccan Plaster | Homebuilding Homebuilding and Renovating
Moroccan Tadelakt: History & Manufacture | 2020-06-17 | Walls & Ceilings Walls & Ceilings logo Walls & Ceilings logo

techniques.markers: Seamless lime plaster with a soft satin-to-glossy sheen and velvety, stone-like depth; mottled, slightly cloudy tone; tinted any color, deep red traditional; faint hairline cracks.

interior.markers: Jointless polished plaster on bathroom walls, baths, sinks and vanities, curving continuously with a soft velvety gleam.

sources.title: Tadelakt: What you Need to Know About Moroccan Plaster | Homebuilding Homebuilding and Renovating

architecture.markers: Smooth burnished lime plaster on exterior facades and hammam walls, with a soft sheen and a mottled tone, traditionally deep red.

sources.title: Moroccan Tadelakt: History & Manufacture | 2020-06-17 | Walls & Ceilings Walls & Ceilings logo Walls & Ceilings logo

techniques.name: Terrazzo casting
techniques.description: A composite of marble, quartz, granite or glass chips in a cement or polymer binder, poured in place or precast, then ground and polished to a uniformly textured floor or wall surface.
techniques.markers: Smooth polished surface densely speckled with multicolored stone or glass chips in a solid ground, often divided by thin metal strips into colored fields, lines or medallions.

techniques.name: Urushi
techniques.description: Lacquering with the refined sap of the urushi tree, applied to a wooden or other base in many thin coats, each dried and polished before the next; often decorated with sprinkled gold or silver maki-e.

sources.title: Urushi: All You Need to Know About Japanese Lacquer

techniques.markers: Polished, hard lacquer in deep black or red, sometimes yellow, green or brown; often fine gold or silver powder designs and mother-of-pearl inlay.

decorative-arts.markers: Bowls, boxes and tea caddies in polished black or red lacquer, decorated in gold powder with plants, seasons and creatures.

sources.title: Urushi: All You Need to Know About Japanese Lacquer

furniture.markers: Cabinets and chests in polished lacquer: black grounds with gold maki-e, or inlays of mother-of-pearl and eggshell.

sources.title: Urushi: All You Need to Know About Japanese Lacquer

fashion.markers: Small hanging cases (inro) in black lacquer with gold maki-e, colored shell inlay and gold foil.

sources.title: Urushi: All You Need to Know About Japanese Lacquer

variants.name: Maki-e
variants.description: Decoration in which gold, silver or copper powder is sprinkled onto designs drawn in wet lacquer, then sealed under further layers of polished transparent lacquer.
variants.markers: Gold and silver powder images on black lacquer: hairline drawing, gradated shading, motifs of plants, birds and seasons, sealed flush under a polished surface.

sources.title: Urushi: All You Need to Know About Japanese Lacquer

variants.name: Negoro
variants.description: Lacquer built from coats of red over black in differing thicknesses, named after the Buddhist monastery where it developed.
variants.markers: Rich red lacquer worn through in places to reveal deep black underneath; use-worn patches across a smooth surface.

sources.title: Urushi: All You Need to Know About Japanese Lacquer
Urushi: All You Need to Know About Japanese Lacquer

techniques.name: Venetian plaster
techniques.description: A lime and marble-dust plaster troweled on in thin layers and burnished, giving walls and ceilings a finish that ranges from matte, stone-like marmorino to glossy, marble-like stucco veneziano.

Dulux Acratex® Venetian Plaster™ Marmorino Naturale | Dulux

techniques.markers: Smooth, dense mineral surface with soft cloudy tonal movement and illusory depth, burnished to a glass-like, marble-like sheen that shifts with light and viewing angle.

interior.markers: Seamless polished plaster on feature walls, ceilings, foyers and dining rooms, reading as tinted marble, sealed with wax to a soft or high sheen.

sources.title: Marmorino vs Venetian Plaster: Key Differences, Uses, and How to Choos | Vasari Lime Plaster & Paint American Express Apple Pay Diners Club Discover Google Pay Mastercard PayPal Shop Pay Visa

variants.name: Marmorino
variants.description: A Venetian lime plaster of slaked lime, coarser marble flour and limestone or sand aggregate, applied in two or three coats and lightly compressed rather than polished to a mirror gloss.
variants.markers: Matte to soft satin stone-like wall with subtle texture and cloudy movement, diffusing light gently for an earthy, calm surface.

sources.title: Marmorino vs Venetian Plaster: Key Differences, Uses, and How to Choos | Vasari Lime Plaster & Paint American Express Apple Pay Diners Club Discover Google Pay Mastercard PayPal Shop Pay Visa

variants.name: Stucco veneziano
variants.description: Venetian plaster of aged slaked lime and very fine marble dust, applied in three to five thin coats and intensively burnished until it resembles polished marble or onyx.
variants.markers: Ultra-smooth, high-gloss, glass-like wall with deep marbled movement and a reflective surface that changes with light.

techniques.name: Wire brushing
techniques.description: Texturing wood by passing wire brushes across the board to remove the softer wood, leaving the harder grain raised; common on oak and hickory flooring.

sources.title: Havwoods USA News | How to Choose the Right Textured Wood Flooring
Choosing Textures for Your Wood Flooring - Real Wood Floors
Bona Wire Brush Technology – Hardwood Floors Magazine

techniques.markers: Wood with hard grain lines standing slightly proud of shallow brushed-out grooves; grain pattern accentuated and tactile; matte or oiled surface where light catches the relief.

interior.markers: Plank floors, often oak, with a brushed raised-grain texture under a matte or oiled finish, hiding scuffs and catching light across the boards.

sources.title: Havwoods USA News | How to Choose the Right Textured Wood Flooring

variants.name: Light wire-brushed
variants.description: A light brushing that removes only a little soft grain, for a subtle texture.
variants.markers: Subtle, refined texture: grain gently emphasized, surface reads as nearly smooth.

sources.title: Choosing Textures for Your Wood Flooring - Real Wood Floors
Havwoods USA News | How to Choose the Right Textured Wood Flooring

variants.name: Severe wire-brushed
variants.description: A heavy brushing that pulls out more soft grain for pronounced texture.
variants.markers: Pronounced raised grain and deeper grooves you can see and feel, giving a rugged plank surface.

sources.title: Choosing Textures for Your Wood Flooring - Real Wood Floors

techniques.name: Yakisugi
techniques.description: Japanese technique of charring the surface of sugi (Japanese cedar) boards to form a protective carbon layer, often brushed and oiled afterwards; also called shou sugi ban.

sources.title: Buyer’s Guide: Yakisugi, Sugi, and Hinoki Wood Products | Nakamoto Forestry
Shou Sugi Ban or Yakisugi? | Popular Woodworking

techniques.markers: Deep black charred cedar boards brushed to a smooth, silky low-sheen finish; a semi-opaque oil coat highlights faint grain lines and subtle burnt-grain shadows across the even char.

architecture.markers: Exterior siding of long charred cedar boards, shiplap or square edge, wrapping walls in a continuous dark textured skin.

sources.title: Buyer’s Guide: Yakisugi, Sugi, and Hinoki Wood Products | Nakamoto Forestry
Shou Sugi Ban or Yakisugi? | Popular Woodworking

interior.markers: Interior wall paneling of charred cedar boards with a smooth, silky dark face, sealed under a polyurethane, alkyd oil or acrylic coat.

sources.title: Buyer’s Guide: Yakisugi, Sugi, and Hinoki Wood Products | Nakamoto Forestry

variants.name: Suyaki
variants.description: Charred boards left unbrushed, keeping the full soot layer.
variants.markers: Thick, dull black soot layer left unbrushed, covering the board face in a heavy layer of charcoal.

sources.title: Buyer’s Guide: Yakisugi, Sugi, and Hinoki Wood Products | Nakamoto Forestry

variants.name: Pika-Pika
variants.description: Charred boards brushed twice to remove most loose soot and expose a textured, striped grain.
variants.markers: Textured surface of striped grain patterns: dark charred stripes alternating with lighter wood where most of the loose soot has been brushed away.

sources.title: Buyer’s Guide: Yakisugi, Sugi, and Hinoki Wood Products | Nakamoto Forestry

variants.name: Gendai
variants.description: Charred boards brushed once to remove the heavy soot, leaving a smooth finish; supplied unoiled or with oil or other coatings.
variants.markers: Smooth, silky, deep black surface with the heavy soot removed.

sources.title: Buyer’s Guide: Yakisugi, Sugi, and Hinoki Wood Products | Nakamoto Forestry
Shou Sugi Ban or Yakisugi? | Popular Woodworking
Shou Sugi Ban or Yakisugi? | Popular Woodworking

effects.name: Antiqued
effects.description: Finish made to look old, usually by sanding paint through at wear points and wiping on a tinted glaze that stays in recesses.

sources.title: Creating An Antiqued, Aged Look for Pieces in Your Home - This Old House Play Play
Faux Finishing Your Woodworking and Furniture Projects | General Finishes

effects.markers: Worn flat paint with darker glaze settled in corners, mouldings and recesses, lighter wiped high spots, and edges sanded through to undercoat or bare wood.

furniture.markers: Cabinets and case pieces sanded through at door edges and around handles, with brown or ochre glaze in panel recesses.

sources.title: Faux Finishing Your Woodworking and Furniture Projects | General Finishes

interior.markers: Beams and woodwork with timeworn painted and glazed surfaces.

sources.title: Creating An Antiqued, Aged Look for Pieces in Your Home - This Old House Play Play

effects.name: Charred
effects.description: Wood surface burnt to a layer of black carbon, left as a heavy char or brushed back to bring out the grain; ranges from lightly toasted to deep black.

architecture.markers: Charred timber cladding, gates and fences: deep black boards with visible grain relief and a textured, weathered face.

variants.description: Char brushed back after burning, removing the softer burnt wood so the harder grain stands in relief.

effects.name: Crackle
effects.description: Network of fine cracks in paint, varnish, lacquer or ceramic glaze, formed by age and shrinkage or produced deliberately as a decorative effect.
effects.markers: Fine web of hairline cracks breaking the surface into small irregular islands; cracks read darker where dirt fills them, especially in light paint.

fine-art.markers: Crack network across paint and varnish: small rectangular blocks on Italian panels, larger curving, irregular cracks on French canvases.

decorative-arts.markers: Deliberate crackle glaze with a dense crack network across the glaze, as on Chinese Ge ware with its double crackle.

effects.name: Distressed
effects.description: Finish deliberately sanded, dented, scraped or rubbed through so a new or refinished object looks aged and worn.

sources.title: How to Distress Furniture: Step-by-Step Guide | RMP Finishes

effects.markers: Paint worn through at edges, corners and touch points to bare wood or an underlayer; scattered dents, divots and wire-brushed grooves; uneven, layered colour.

furniture.markers: Painted tables, sideboards and cabinets sanded back at edges and corners, with dents and grooves and earlier paint layers showing.

sources.title: How to Distress Furniture: Step-by-Step Guide | RMP Finishes

variants.name: Dry-brushed
variants.description: Distressed look made by dragging a nearly dry brush of paint over a painted surface.
variants.markers: Thin, streaky brushed paint over a base coat, giving a lightly weathered look.

effects.name: Patina
effects.description: Thin surface film or mellowed change in colour and texture that age, exposure, wear and handling give metal, stone, wood and leather.

sources.title: Should you remove patina from antiques? | Homes and Antiques

effects.markers: Softened, uneven colour and gentle sheen: green to brown films on copper alloys, darkened stone, a worn glow on handled wood and leather.

furniture.markers: Antique chests and leather chairs with worn, mellowed surfaces at touch points instead of a high polish.

sources.title: Should you remove patina from antiques? | Homes and Antiques

effects.name: Polished
effects.description: Surface abraded with progressively finer grits until smooth and shiny, giving strong specular reflection.

sources.title: Stone Selection 101: Polished vs. Honed Stone Finishes - Coldspring
The Texture of Luxury: Honed vs Polished Marble Explained

effects.markers: Glossy, mirror-like face reflecting light; on stone the full colour depth, veining and crystal structure appear vivid and saturated.

interior.markers: High-gloss marble floors in entries, fireplace surrounds and feature walls that reflect light and brighten the room.

sources.title: The Texture of Luxury: Honed vs Polished Marble Explained

effects.name: Rusted
effects.description: Iron or steel covered with reddish-brown iron oxide, from flaky, friable surface rust to the dense, adherent patina of weathering steel.

Specifying Cor-ten for External Architectural Use | Marshalls

effects.markers: Orange to reddish-brown and dark brown oxide, matte and textured; loose rust porous and flaking, weathering steel a warm dark brown.

architecture.markers: Weathering steel cladding, planters, seating and lighting columns in a matt rust-brown, sometimes with rust stains on adjacent paving.

sources.title: Specifying Cor-ten for External Architectural Use | Marshalls
Weathering steel – Guide to corrosion-resistant steels - SSAB

variants.description: Steel alloyed to form a dense, adherent rust patina that seals the surface and needs no paint.

effects.description: Colour faded and lightened by long sun exposure, turning wood a weathered grey; imitated on new wood with grey or whitewash stains.

effects.markers: Pale, washed-out grey driftwood tone with grain showing through a soft, light finish, palest at worn edges and corners.

furniture.markers: Wood furniture in a light grey or whitewashed driftwood tone, softened at edges and corners.

effects.name: Verdigris
effects.description: Green to bluish-green copper salt patina that forms on copper, brass and bronze, and a historic green pigment made from it.

effects.markers: Turquoise, green and blue-green surface over copper, brass or bronze; the bright bluish green of aged domes, statues and lanterns.

sources.title: Why the natural patina that forms on copper, brass, and bronze is the colour of timelessness | Country Life logo logo
